Prevention: Clean the storage facility and burn all sweepings
Paint the storage facility white to make insect pests easy to detect
Ensure that grains are clean and well-dried before storing.
Dry in sun for 1 month or until 7-10% moisture
Put properly dried cowpea grains in air-tight container, filling the container to the brim [short- time storage]
Store bags on pallets to raise them off the floor
Stack bags for more effective fumigation, if necessary later
Monitoring: Look for beetles on the bags or directly on the grains
Look for holes in the grains
Look for larvae (tumbu) on the grains
Look for powder or dust in the bag.
This is the crumbs created by the tumbu feeding on the grains
Direct Control: Mix 5ml of groundnut oil to 1kg of cowpea grains and store in air-tight containers [short-time storage]
Add 1500g of dried chili to one bag of dried cowpea grains [long-time storage]
Disinfect storage facility and bags with pirimiphos- methyl
Disinfect storage facility and bags with diazinon or chlorpyriphos
Restrictions: Very toxic if swallowed or inhaled
Following fumigation, wait 6 months before consumption or sale
Wrap the aluminium phosphide tablet in a piece of cloth, tissue paper, or perforated envelope before placing inside the container
